articles.text: ĀNDÉSĒN XIĀNSHENG: Qǐngwèn, nǐmen zhèli kěyi huàn Měijīn ma?
MR. ANDERSON: May I ask, can U.S. currency be changed here?
DIÀNYUÁN: Duìbuqǐ, bù kěyi. Nín děi zài Táiwān Yínháng huàn.
SHOP ASSISTANT: I'm sorry, that's not possible. You have to change it at the Bank of Taiwan.
ĀNDÉSĒN XIĀNSHENG: Yínháng shénme shíhou kāi mén?
MR. ANDERSON: When does the bank open?
DIÀNYUÁN: Zǎoshang jiǔdiǎn zhōng kāi mén, xiàwǔ sāndiǎn zhōng guān mén.
SHOP ASSISTANT: It opens at nine in the morning and closes at three in the afternoon.
ĀNDÉSĒN XIĀNSHENG: Xiànzài jǐdiǎn zhōng? Hái kěyi huàn ba?
MR. ANDERSON: What time is it now? I may still change money, I suppose?
DIÀNYUÁN: Xiànzài liǎngdiǎn bàn. Hái kěyi huàn.
SHOP ASSISTANT: It's half past two now. You may still change money.
ĀNDÉSĒN XIĀNSHENG: Hǎo. Máfan ni le.
MR. ANDERSON: Good. Sorry to have bothered you.
